cards.text: Jesus has just been baptized, and a voice from heaven said, “You are My beloved Son; in You I am well pleased.” (Luke 3:21-22) Now Jesus, full of the Holy Spirit, heads back from the Jordan, and the Spirit leads Him somewhere new.

cards.question: Full of the Holy Spirit, Jesus is led by the Spirit into the ___.

cards.text: Out there, for forty days, the devil tempts Him, and Jesus eats nothing the whole time. FORTY days, friend, and I can't make it forty minutes past the timer without sneaking a cookie off the rack.

cards.question: When the forty days of eating nothing in the wilderness are over, Jesus is hungry.

cards.text: So the devil, who's been tempting Him this whole time, steps up to a hungry Jesus with a dare.

cards.question: The devil says to Jesus, “If You are the Son of God, tell this stone to become ___.”
Hungry Jesus is staring at a stone the devil wants turned into bread. How does He answer?

answers.text: He answers with what is written
He turns the stone into bread

cards.text: Jesus answers, “It is written: ‘Man shall not live on bread alone.’” Forty days hungry and He still says no, while I once lost an argument with a single chocolate chip.
Round two. The devil leads Jesus up to a high place and shows Him all the kingdoms of the world in an instant, and then he makes an offer.

cards.question: Up on that high place, the devil offers Jesus authority over all the kingdoms of the world and all their glory.
The devil claims those kingdoms were handed over to him. What does he want from Jesus in return for all of them?
Jesus answers the devil's offer with Scripture again. Who does it say to worship and serve?

cards.text: Round three. The devil takes Jesus to Jerusalem, sets Him on the pinnacle of the temple, and dares Him: if You are the Son of God, throw Yourself down from here.

cards.question: Jesus keeps answering the devil with what is written. So this time the devil backs up his dare with ___ of his own.

cards.text: He says it's written that angels will guard Jesus carefully and lift Him up in their hands, so He won't strike His foot against a stone. Wait. WAIT. The devil is quoting Scripture now?

cards.question: Jesus answers the devil's quote with another line of Scripture. What does it say not to do?

answers.text: Put the Lord your God to the test
Climb up to the highest places
Ask the angels to rescue you

cards.text: Jesus answers, “It also says, ‘Do not put the Lord your God to the test.’” Three dares, and three answers straight from what is written.

cards.question: When the devil had finished every temptation, he left Jesus for good.

cards.text: When the devil has finished every temptation, he leaves Jesus until an opportune time. Not gone for good, friend. Just gone for now.

findings.problem: Stop 1, card 6 quotes "If You are the Son of God, tell this stone to become ___.", which isn't the exact BSB wording.

rule.text: Quotes: Quotation marks around Bible words mean the exact BSB wording, punctuation included.

findings.problem: "Forty days hungry" says Jesus was hungry for all forty days. Luke 4:2 says He ate nothing during those days, and He was hungry when they had ended. This is a Scripture statement, not part of the joke, so it stretches the text.

rule.text: Don't stretch the text. Exaggerate only in his own jokes.

findings.problem: The card tells that the devil "makes an offer," which happens in Luke 4:6. The card cites only Luke 4:5.

rule.text: Every story card cites the verses it tells, from the first verse it uses to the last, no wider and no narrower.

findings.problem: "The devil claims those kingdoms were handed over to him." In Luke 4:6 the devil says "it has been relinquished to me," and "it" refers to the authority and glory, not the kingdoms themselves. The card renames what the text says was relinquished.

rule.text: Call things what the text calls them.

findings.problem: "Jesus keeps answering the devil with what is written. So this time the devil backs up his dare..." gives a reason for the devil quoting Scripture that Luke 4:9-11 doesn't give. "Scripture of his own" also makes the quoted Scripture sound like it belongs to the devil.

rule.text: He never adds why someone did, said or thought something unless the text says why.

findings.problem: The wrong answer "angels" is arguable. The devil's quote in Luke 4:10-11 is about angels guarding and lifting Jesus, so a baker could argue that he backs up his dare with angels.

rule.text: A wrong answer never means the same as the right answer, or close to it. If a baker could argue it's right, replace it.

findings.problem: The card opens with "He says," with no name. Card 14 is no longer on screen, and a capitalized He elsewhere in this walkthrough means Jesus, so it isn't clear the devil is the one quoting.

rule.text: Short, but not stripped down. A story card still has enough of Papa Dorin's voice and enough context that the moment makes sense.

findings.problem: The right answer "Put the Lord your God to the test" is the only one in Bible wording. The wrong answers "Climb up to the highest places" and "Ask the angels to rescue you" don't sound like Scripture, so the right answer stands out.

rule.text: Don't let the right answer stand out. All the answers should sound alike. None should sound more like the Bible, or more modern, than the others.

findings.problem: "Three dares" doesn't match what the text calls them. Luke 4:13 calls them temptations, and the second one was an offer (card 9 even calls it an offer), not a dare.

rule.text: Call things what the text calls them.

findings.problem: Most story cards (1, 5, 9, 13, 17, 19) are plain retelling with no Papa Dorin voice. The only two jokes (cards 3 and 8) are the same self-deprecating bit about not resisting cookies. The walkthrough reads like a pleasant narrator, not laugh-out-loud funny.

rule.text: If a line reads like a nice dad being pleasant, push it further.
